correctness.rationale: At each fully receptive step opinion vector equals P^t x0 and edge bounds c_t=1-(1-c)(1-gamma)^t. Finite Kantorovich-Rubinstein duality equals max edge-Lipschitz amplification of P^t to Lambda_G(t); diameter bound cD<=1 makes its extremizing scaled Lipschitz witness a valid [0,1] profile, giving necessity, not merely sufficiency. For K_{1,k}, centered leaf-hub differences evolve by B_k=I/2-J/(k+1), norm 3(k-1)/(2(k+1)), B_k^2=I/4-J/(k+1)^2 with norm <=1/3 for k>=2, so t>=2 never creates a new obstruction. The t=1 inequality yields gamma*, with a strictly interior extremal sign vector showing rupture for k>=6 and any gamma<gamma*. k=1 has B=0. Reversible irreducible lazy walk P preserves weights deg+1, giving consensus.
residual_risks: Necessity of the general graph criterion requires c<=1/D; sufficiency needs no such bound.
Star threshold proven for c<=1/2 (special one-edge star 0<c<1), initially fully receptive edges, synchronous self-inclusive averaging; rupture is not asserted irreversible.
The original model and graph-transport duality are pre-existing; historical priority of the exact phase threshold is qualified.
